page: Microsoft Azure E64d_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. It is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled, consisting of 2458 GB of local disk space.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput. The server achieves top-tier results in multi-threaded tasks, including stress-ng multi-core CPU performance, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient for large blocks, reaching 298.57 GB/sec for read operations and 130.67 GB/sec for write operations. However, single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores, remains in the average tier.

This hardware profile is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and large-scale data processing. It demonstrates strong performance in Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, processing 62.33 million operations per second. The bundled 2458 GB local storage supports high-throughput local caching and temporary database storage. While it handles small and medium LLM inference tasks adequately, it exhibits weak performance in text generation for large 70B models, indicating it is not optimal for heavy generative AI workloads without GPU acceleration.
description: The Microsoft Azure E64d_v5 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, paired with 512.0 GB of RAM and 2458 GB of bundled local storage. Benchmarks show strong multi-core CPU performance, high memory bandwidth for large blocks, and excellent database capabilities, as evidenced by high Redis SET operations and Passmark database scores. Conversely, single-core performance and large-scale LLM text generation are weaker. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for memory-heavy, data-dense workloads, making it an appropriate choice for relational databases, in-memory caching, and multi-threaded data processing applications.
